title: Wise Consultation Office / RVMN
text:
Wise Consultation Office / RVMN

It is said that trees sway in order not to be shaken. Because they move with flexibility, they are able to remain rooted in their place and continue to grow over time. Marriage, too, is a journey that can be calm at times and shift in unexpected directions, and therefore requires a flexible attitude. In the first WISE space, this perspective on marriage and the idea of flexibility were translated into a design language. Flexible curves and spatial flows were used to create both direct and indirect separation between the circulation and sightlines of waiting customers and those receiving consultations, preventing them from directly interfering with one another.

title: Pinewood Houses / NOMO STUDIO
text:
Pinewood Houses / NOMO STUDIO

Set in a small village on Spain's northern Mediterranean coast, Pinewood Houses comprises two single-family homes embedded within a pine forest near the beach on the Costa Brava. The project is guided by a clear premise: to place the two dwellings in an intercalated arrangement that avoids mutual obstruction, allowing each house to breathe and maintaining long visual depth across the site.

title: Ība House / Daniel Fromer
text:
Ība House / Daniel Fromer

The landscape designer Rodrigo Oliveira was enchanted by a plot of just over five thousand square meters in southern Bahia. With a topography reminiscent of a natural amphitheater, facing the landscape and offering a privileged view of the sunset, Casa ĪBA nestles among natural and designed gardens, always respecting the original topography of the site.

title: L'AIGUILLEUSE - Renovation of a former railway signal box into a kiosk-bar / Studio Téré
text:
L'AIGUILLEUSE - Renovation of a former railway signal box into a kiosk-bar / Studio Téré

"L'Aiguilleuse" is a project that transforms a former 1960s railway signal box into a small kiosk-bar located at the heart of the Jardins de l'Estuaire, a new public park on the Île de Nantes, France. Originally part of the Nantes-État railway infrastructure, the building once controlled train movements entering the station. As the surrounding railway landscape gradually disappeared, the signal box remained as a small but distinctive fragment of the site's industrial history.

title: Chaume Sublimé / COAT
text:
Chaume Sublimé / COAT

Chaume Sublimé is an ephemeral installation for Montpellier's Festival des Architectures Vives 2025 that elevates humble reed grass into a sensory and atmospheric experience, celebrating both sustainability and craftsmanship.

title: Designing the In-Between: From Tactical Interventions to Urban Policy in Barcelona
text:
Designing the In-Between: From Tactical Interventions to Urban Policy in Barcelona

In Europe, cities are confronting the challenge of adapting existing urban conditions to a changing climate and warming summers while improving access to nature, quality public spaces, and the resources of everyday routines. ReGreeneration, a Horizon Europe initiative working across nine European cities, approaches this challenge through urban renaturing at the neighborhood scale. Combining strategies for complete neighborhoods, communal spaces, and nature-based solutions for cities, the Barcelona project examines how climate adaptation is embedded within residual, peripheral spaces of daily life. As part of a series following ReGreeneration across the participating cities, this article turns to Barcelona, where the project is working in the Trinitat Nova neighborhood to explore how small, often overlooked, urban spaces contribute to broader models of regeneration.

title: Home Herengracht / Studio Modijefsky
text:
Home Herengracht / Studio Modijefsky

Nestled in central Amsterdam on the prestigious Herengracht, this canal-side apartment enjoys expansive views over the water while remaining sheltered by the lush trees surrounding the façade. Studio Modijefsky was commissioned to redesign the entrance sequence, guest facilities, kitchen, and pantry, while refining the circulation towards the private quarters of the home. The result is an interior that balances bold material gestures with a calm and timeless spatial experience.

title: RESONANCE - Tallinn Architecture Biennale Installation / Aru Ma- Architects
text:
RESONANCE - Tallinn Architecture Biennale Installation / Aru Ma- Architects

Set against Tallinn's rapidly commercializing urban backdrop, the installation offers a sheltered courtyard detached from its surroundings, creating a deliberate pause. Here, the sea breeze whispers against silent stones, and sunlight filters onto the warm, sweeping curves of plywood screens. It is a spatial privilege carved from ordinary materials, filtering out external chaos for pure atmospheric luxury.

title: Mahachai Residence / Patara Architects
text:
Mahachai Residence / Patara Architects

Mahachai Residence occupies a riverside plot on the Tha Chin River, on land once occupied by the owner's boat-repair warehouse. Rather than erase this history, the house is conceived as a day-use villa, a place for the owner to rest, take in the river, and watch it turn gold at sunset, quietly carrying the memory of the site's working past into its structure and materials.

title: Prukpirom House Renovation (PPR House) / S+S Architects
text:
Prukpirom House Renovation (PPR House) / S+S Architects

Prukpirom House Renovation transforms a family home that has stood for more than 29 years. Located on a generous site surrounded by mature greenery, the existing house offered opportunities to expand and reorganize the living spaces while retaining its relationship with the garden.

title: La Negrita House / Estudio Palacios
text:
La Negrita House / Estudio Palacios

Situated on the shores of Los Molinos Lake and surrounded by a dense eucalyptus forest, La Negrita embodies the desire for a peaceful retreat amid a beautiful, playful atmosphere with its own unique microclimate.

title: Haras House / Felipe Hess Arquitetos
text:
Haras House / Felipe Hess Arquitetos

The Haras House is a single-story residence built on a trapezoidal lot. The "C" shaped volume organizes the spaces around a central courtyard, which features a garden, a porch, and a 25-meter lane, integrated into the resident's daily routine. The design prioritizes privacy and the direct relationship between internal and external spaces.

title: CASA MG / Startup Architettura
text:
CASA MG / Startup Architettura

Located within a 1930s residential building, Casa MG reinterprets and elevates some of the period's most distinctive and iconic architectural features, making them a recurring design language at the heart of the apartment's spatial reorganization.

title: Childcare Centre Mowgli / Natrufied Architecture
text:
Childcare Centre Mowgli / Natrufied Architecture

In the heart of the wooded surroundings of Vught, a unique childcare centre has emerged: Mowgli Childcare Centre. The project combines playful architecture with a strong connection to nature, creating an inspiring environment for young children.

title: The Future as Propaganda: Soviet Architecture in Kazakhstan and the Imagery of a New Era
text:
The Future as Propaganda: Soviet Architecture in Kazakhstan and the Imagery of a New Era

Practically every history book records 1961 as the year man first reached space, an achievement that placed the Soviet Union at the center of the space race. What not everyone knows is that Yuri Gagarin's journey began in a seemingly unlikely place, more precisely in Kazakhstan. From the Baikonur Cosmodrome, Gagarin set off beyond Earth, inaugurating not only a new era of space exploration but also a history of technology and ambition that would transform this landscape.

title: An unfinished domestic device as a threshold between interior and landscape / EX.
text:
An unfinished domestic device as a threshold between interior and landscape / EX.

On the hills of Turin, EX. designs an unfinished house conceived as a domestic device rather than a completed object. A rough concrete perimeter frames an open, adaptable interior where architecture and landscape continuously overlap.

title: Wiki World Forest Store / Wiki World
text:
Wiki World Forest Store / Wiki World

The birth of the Wiki World Forest Store stems from the ongoing natural architecture practice carried out by Wiki World. Although we have always insisted on building with the zeroprint concept and 100% timber structures, along with the birth of one wilderness home after another, there is always wood that inevitably becomes waste. Who wants to be abandoned leftover scraps? So we wondered: could waste materials be used to build a house? Could leftover scraps also have unrealistic fantasies and be turned into interesting wooden products? Therefore, we planned this building and the products inside it. The Wiki World Forest Store is located at the entrance of Merryda Wiki World-Secret Camp, at the edge of a forest. Pure wood and glass are connected, and the recyclable concept does not require more complex craftsmanship.

title: Gutiérrez Café / Toro Arquitectos
text:
Gutiérrez Café / Toro Arquitectos

Gutiérrez Café opened its doors in August 2025, in the Pocitos neighborhood of Montevideo, with an architectural design that places both design and product quality at the heart of the experience. More than just a coffee shop, it is a space carefully conceived to articulate a sensory and urban experience, where architecture becomes an integral part of the gastronomic offering.

title: House D+J / Pablo Lanza Arquitetura
text:
House D+J / Pablo Lanza Arquitetura

In a large plot of land very well chosen by this beautiful family, the initial request and main importance for the project was to maximize the open areas and prioritize greenery.

title: Comillas Waterfront Promenade / Hector Navarro + ARKHITEKTON
text:
Comillas Waterfront Promenade / Hector Navarro + ARKHITEKTON

The intervention transforms an area previously occupied by a narrow sidewalk and a large parking lot into a new public space for Comillas. Rather than refurbishing an existing promenade, the project creates a new seafront, reclaiming an exceptional stretch of coastline for pedestrians and incorporating it into the town's network of public spaces.

title: G – 5 Houses / SUMMARY
text:
G – 5 Houses / SUMMARY

The project is based on total prefabrication in reinforced concrete. Modular panels make up all the building elements: façades, roofs and interior partitions. The typification of elements made it possible to speed up and simplify the construction, while emphasising the building's image.

title: Data Center ETH Zurich / Penzel Valier
text:
Data Center ETH Zurich / Penzel Valier

With the Hönggerberg Data Center (HRZ), Penzel Valier has created an integrated building for ETH Zurich's digital infrastructure in which structure, building services, and design were conceived together from the outset. It houses the server, storage, and communication systems of IT Services and various departments. Complementing the Central Campus data centers within ETH's long-term digital strategy, it replaces several dispersed, outdated facilities and is designed for future expansion.

title: Architecture of Care: 6 Unbuilt Spaces for Childhood from the ArchDaily Community
text:
Architecture of Care: 6 Unbuilt Spaces for Childhood from the ArchDaily Community

As cities change, so do our expectations of them. People are asking for more caring spaces: public places open to all ages and genders, nature within reach of every social class, and settings that foster connection. Few design intentions hold these together as well as spaces for children. This selection of unbuilt projects submitted by ArchDaily readers showcases different approaches to care-based architecture. Schools, daycare centers, a library, a youth center, and a new model for orphanages take on the mission of providing a safe and stimulating environment for children at every stage of their development. Not yet built but carefully designed, these proposals offer a glimpse into spaces for play, learning, and calm that fuel creativity in design for people of all ages.

title: House in Tinos  / Kelly Spanou
text:
House in Tinos / Kelly Spanou

House is Tinos is the renovation and extension of a 115-square-metre residence on the island of Tinos, developed across two levels that follow the natural inclination of the terrain. The project works with the building's existing irregularities, material imperfections, and traces of different periods of construction, embracing these conditions rather than attempting to erase them.
